case_name: Ajit Singh and Others v State of Punjab and Another
respondent:
State of Punjab and Another
Supreme Court of India

10 March 1983
W.P. (Civil) Nos. 5274-81, 5463, 5348 & 5606 of 1980
The Judgment was delivered by : D. A. Desai, J.
1. These writ petitions u/art. 32 of the Constitution questioned the validity of the orders dispensing with service of each of the petitioner with immediate effect made by the Director Local Government. Punjab dated September 25, 1980 as being violative of Arts. 14 and 16 of the Constitution.
2. facts: The writ petitions questioned the validity of the orders dispensing with service of each of the petitioners with immediate effect made by the Director Local Government, Punjab dated September 25, 1980 as being violative of Arts. 14 and 16 of the Constitution.
The Punjab Town Improvement Act, 1922 ('Act for short) was enacted to make provision for the improvement and expansion of towns in Punjab.
One such service contemplated by the s. was Punjab Service of Trust-Executive officers.

Rule 5 (2) (i) inter alia provided that fifty percent of the vacancies in the cadre of Executive officers shall be filled by direct recruitment and for this purpose rule 5(4) envisaged the setting up of a Selection Committee called Punjab Trust Services Selection Committee.
The Punjab Trust Services Selection Committee interviewed various candidates and ultimately recommended eleven persons for the post of Trust Executive officers.
Each one of the appointees was issued an order of appointment to which terms and conditions of appointment were annexed.
One such condition worth- noticing reads as under: 'All the appointees shall remain on probation for a period of one year under rule 10 (1) of the Rules.'
After each appointee completed one year of service, an increment was released in his favour.
Director of Local Government, Punjab dispensed with the service of each of the 11 Trust Executive officers, who were appointed on May 28, 1979.
These orders are impugned in these petitions.

The State Government decided to dispense with the services of those Executive officers appointed by direct recruitment who had not completed the probationary period of 2 years under Rule 9 (1) of '1978 Rules'.

It was contended that all the petitioners were appointed through direct recruitment as Executive officers in the Punjab Trust Services on May 28, 1979 and according to the respondents the period of probation was two years which would expire on May 27, 1981.
Explaining why one month pay in lieu of notice was paid, it was contended that payment was ex majorie cautela and it can confer no right on the petitioners.
It was lastly contended that as the Trusts were dissolved, the services of the petitioners as Executive officers had become surplus and therefore, had to be dispensed with as a compelling necessity.
issues: What is the period of probation in respect of each of the appointee?
Can the State Government terminate the service of the petitioners in the manner in which it is done?
Were the actions taken by the State Government arbitrary and violative of equality of opportunity in the matter of employment?
petitioner_arguments: All the appointees shall remain on probation for a period of one year under rule 10 (1) of the Rules.
The regular appointments shall be subject to the satisfactory completion of the probation period by such appointee after the expiry of one year from the date of his joining.
After each appointee completed one year of service, an increment was released in his favour.

It is also challenged on the additional ground that after the completion of the period of probation it was not open to the State Government to terminate the service of the petitioners, in the manner in which it is done.

One more ground of attack was that the Action was malafide in that the petitioners were appointed when a political party of other hue and colour was in power and on a change of Government, the petitioners were victimised.

court_reasoning: The real question in controversy was what was the period of probation in respect of each of the appointee.

It is not in dispute nor is it controverter by the respondents that the appointment order issued by the Punjab Government did recite that the person mentioned in the order is appointed to Punjab Trust Services of Executive officers Class I or Class II or 111 as the case may be subject to the conditions annexed to the order etc.
Nowhere A in the affidavit in opposition, the respondents state as to whether rule 10 (1) also confers power to prescribe a period of probation.
Reference is to Rule 9 (1) which prescribed a period of probation of two years for those appointed by direct recruitment.
All the petitioners were appointed by direct recruitment.
